transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep getting up when I’m supposed to stay seated. It happens during client interviews, tutoring sessions, even book club. I’ll tell myself to just sit and listen, but I end up standing or moving around, and people are starting to notice.
Do you often feel restless or have the urge to move even when you’re trying to stay still?

Yes. Especially when I’m stuck at the computer going through records. My foot will be bouncing under the desk, or I’ll be clicking a pen without realizing it. I shift around a lot too, and sometimes I move so much I lose my place in what I’m reading.
Do these restlessness and movement issues happen in other settings as well, like at home or in social situations?

Yes, it happens outside work too. At home or in social stuff, even things that are supposed to be quiet, like yoga or reading at book club, I have a hard time just being still. I’ll start whispering little comments, rustling papers, or making some excuse to get up and move around. It’s frustrating because those things used to help me calm down.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or staying attentive, especially during tasks that require sustained mental effort, like reading or working on a project?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I can usually do the work if I need to, but I haven’t paid as much attention to whether it’s focus specifically. It’s more that I notice myself getting physically unsettled when I’m supposed to sit through something.
Can you think of times when you’ve had trouble keeping your attention on a task, like missing details or getting distracted easily, even if you were trying to focus?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed it as missing details or being distracted in that way. I can think of feeling antsy during tasks, but whether my attention is actually slipping… I don’t know. I’d have to think about that more.

Can you think of specific times when you've had difficulty staying focused, such as finding yourself daydreaming, missing what someone said in a conversation, or needing to reread things because your mind wandered?

I can’t really think of a clear example like that. I don’t usually catch myself daydreaming or missing whole chunks of what someone said. If I reread something, I’m not sure if it’s because my mind wandered or because I’m just physically restless and trying to get through it. So… I’m not sure I can say that’s been a noticeable problem for me.
Have you noticed any situations where you have difficulty waiting your turn, interrupt others, or say things without thinking?

Yes, that does happen. At work, if I hear the junior detectives talking through a lead, I’ll jump in with questions or advice before anyone’s asked me. And even outside work, like if a neighbor is talking in the hallway, I sometimes butt in before I really think about whether it’s my conversation to join. Then afterward I realize, okay, I kind of barged in there.

Can you think of other times when you've acted quickly without thinking through the consequences, like making sudden decisions, spending impulsively, or jumping into something before it was your turn?

Mostly it’s the jumping into conversations before I’ve really thought it through. Like if I hear the junior detectives talking over a lead, I’ll step in with questions or advice before anyone’s asked me. Or even with a neighbor in the hallway, I’ll kind of insert myself into the conversation.

Then afterward I realize, yeah, I barged in there and probably should’ve waited.

Can you think of times when you had trouble staying focused on tasks, like being easily distracted by things around you, or finding it hard to follow through on instructions or chores, even if they weren’t difficult?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that much. If a task is straightforward, I can usually follow it through. I don’t really have examples of getting distracted by things around me or not finishing chores because I couldn’t focus. It’s more that I get restless sometimes, but I can’t say it’s a focus problem in the way you’re describing.

Can you think of times when you started a task but had trouble finishing it, even if it was something simple like sending an email or putting away dishes, because your mind felt disorganized or you lost track of what you were doing?

I can’t really think of that happening much. If I start something simple like an email or putting dishes away, I usually finish it. I don’t have a clear example where my mind got disorganized and I lost track of what I was doing.

Can you think of times when you found it hard to follow along with what someone was saying, not because you were physically restless, but because your mind was elsewhere or you were easily pulled away by other thoughts?

Not really, no. I mean, if someone’s talking to me, I usually can follow what they’re saying. I might get impatient sometimes, but I don’t think my mind is drifting off or getting pulled away by other thoughts in a way that makes me lose the thread.
Can you think of times when you had trouble concentrating or found your mind going blank, even when you weren’t feeling physically restless or needing to move?

I don’t think so. I mean, I might have the usual moments where I pause or need a second, but I wouldn’t say my mind goes blank or that I can’t concentrate when I’m sitting still. I haven’t really noticed that as a problem.
Can you think of times when these restlessness and impulsivity issues have affected you in different areas of your life, like at home, at work, and in social situations?

Yes. Work is where it shows up the most. I’m a private investigator, so details matter, and I’ve missed things because I’m moving too fast or reacting too quickly. I’ve had clients get irritated with me, and some of the junior detectives don’t really want to debrief with me because they feel like I steamroll them.  

At home and socially it comes up too, but professionally is where it’s starting to cost me.
Looking back, were you already someone who had trouble staying still or acted impulsively as a child, or did these behaviors start more recently?

It definitely goes back to when I was a kid. My grade-school report cards always had some version of, “She’s bright, but she can’t stay in her seat,” or “needs to wait her turn.” My mother still jokes that I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through. So no, it’s not something that just started recently.
Can you tell me more about how these behaviors have affected your work and other areas of your life? Specifically, have they caused problems with relationships, job performance, or daily tasks?

Yeah, it’s mostly showing up at work. It’s starting to cost me professionally. I’ve missed details in investigations because I move too quickly or jump ahead, and that’s obviously not great in my line of work.

It’s also affected relationships there. Some clients have gotten irritated with me, and a few of the junior detectives don’t really like debriefing with me because they feel like I talk over them or steamroll the conversation. I don’t mean to, but I can see how it comes across.
